The method

Original study and code for The Vibes Are People. Seeded directions sit on a grid; smooth interpolation blends the neighboring vectors. Each path follows that field with a limited turn at each step.

Recipe and reproduction details

Algorithm: interpolated-direction-field-v1. A 32-bit seeded random stream sets the field and starting points. Every path takes up to 160 steps of 2.6 pixels, ending at the drawing margin. Density sets the path count; field scale sets grid spacing; turning sets the maximum angle change per step.

This implementation uses interpolated random vectors, not Perlin noise, curl noise, or a fluid solver. The version 1 recipe stores the seed, all three parameters, the fixed canvas, and frame: null for this static drawing. Reproduction is deterministic within the same browser; Canvas antialiasing can differ across browsers. Imports must match this version and canvas and be at most 16 KB.

People and context

Tyler Hobbs, Flow Fields (2020) explains tracing curves through direction grids and varying their behavior. That essay is contextual reading; this demo is an original implementation, not a reconstruction of his artwork.
